transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is I can’t keep my mind on the thing in front of me lately. Like when I’m driving, every CB chirp, every fuel price sign, some new idea popping in my head—my attention just jumps.

And I’ve been missing stuff I normally don’t miss. Delivery notes from clients, who I said I’d call back… little things, but they matter in my work. I’ve been driving a long time, you know, and I usually keep all that straight. I was just talking to a guy last week about diesel prices—anyway, yeah, it’s like my head won’t stay on one channel.
Have you noticed yourself being more active than usual, like doing more things at once, feeling like you have extra energy, or not needing as much sleep lately?

Yeah… yeah, I guess I have been doing more. I keep sort of finding extra jobs for myself, like rewriting route plans that were already fine, checking in on the newer drivers after hours, that kind of thing.

And at home too, I’ll start fixing some little thing around the house and then notice three other things. My wife’ll be watching TV and I’m up messing with a cabinet hinge or reorganizing tools. I don’t know if it’s “extra energy” exactly, but I get real antsy if I sit still too long.
Do you find that you're easily distracted or have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations lately? Like your attention shifts quickly to unrelated things?

Yeah, that’s exactly it. It’s like my attention just won’t stay put. I’ll be listening to somebody, or trying to read a delivery note, and then the CB makes a noise or I see a fuel price sign and my head is off somewhere else.

That’s kind of what finally got me to come in, honestly. I’ve been missing little details I normally never miss—like a client’s note on a drop-off, or I’ll forget who I told I’d call back. And I’ve been doing this work long enough that I usually keep that stuff straight. It’s frustrating, because it’s not like me.
Have you had any periods where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, for several days in a row?

I mean… I don’t know. I have off days, sure, everybody does. Like if a load runs late or something breaks on the truck, that’ll put me in a mood, and then I’ll come home grumbling about it.

But several days in a row where I felt hopeless or stopped caring about things? I can’t really say I’ve noticed that. I guess I haven’t been paying attention to it that way.
Have you had any times recently where your mood felt unusually high, like you were really wired, irritable, or on top of the world, even if just for a few days?

Yeah… I guess “wired” is probably the word. For a few months now I’ll get this thing where I’m all fired up, like I’ve got it all figured out and everything’s gonna work out fine no matter what. Like I’m ahead of the game somehow.

But then other times it flips and I’m just irritated over nothing. My wife’ll ask me something normal, or someone in the yard does something small, and I’m snapping before I even think about it. That’s not really how I usually am. I mean, I get annoyed like anybody, but this has felt… sharper, I guess. More than it should be.
Can you describe how long these 'wired' or irritable periods last? Like, do they come and go, or have they been pretty much constant?

It’s been… I’d say about seven months? Around when my daughter moved back home. That’s when I started trying to keep everything steady, you know—making sure the house didn’t turn into a whole big mess, everybody getting along, bills and schedules and all that.

So it’s not like one afternoon here and there. It kind of comes and goes inside that stretch, but this whole wired-up or irritable thing has been hanging around since then.
